record.paper_title: Some open problems in Banach space theory
record.original_question: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional Banach space X such that every bounded linear operator T: X → X can be written in the form T = λI + K, where λ is a scalar, I is the identity operator on X, and K is a compact operator?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$ such that every bounded linear operator $T \colon X \to X$ can be written in the form $T = \lambda I + K$, where $\lambda$ is a scalar, $I$ is the identity operator on $X$, and $K \colon X \to X$ is a compact operator?
artifact.status_search_result: The scalar-plus-compact problem was solved affirmatively by S. A. Argyros and R. G. Haydon (2009/2011), who constructed a hereditarily indecomposable Bourgain–Delbaen-type Banach space with dual isomorphic to ℓ₁ on which every bounded linear operator is of the form λI + K with K compact.

status_evidence.title: A hereditarily indecomposable L_∞-space that solves the scalar-plus-compact problem
status_evidence.snippet: Argyros and Haydon construct an infinite-dimensional Banach space on which every bounded operator has the form λI + K.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is solved affirmatively by Argyros and Haydon.

status_evidence.title: On the Solution of the Scalar-plus-compact Problem by Argyros and Haydon
status_evidence.snippet: Exposition of the Argyros–Haydon solution to the scalar-plus-compact problem posed by Lindenstrauss.
